Category or scenario: Note on colposcopy rule extraction
Source document: Detailed extraction prepared from scanned colposcopy guide
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: The rows below reflect a detailed transcription and normalization of the booking-priority guide. Please confirm whether these interpretations match local practice and amend any wording or timing that differs.
What information does the grader need to: HPV result, HPV group, cytology group, immune status, referral context, repeat or prior history

Category or scenario: Primary screening: HPV 16/18 with cytology reporting suspicion or definite cancer
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HPV 16/18 with cytology reporting suspicion or definite cancer -> 10 days.
What information does the grader need to: HPV genotype and cytology result

Category or scenario: Primary screening: HPV 16/18 with or without cytology, any cytology excluding cancer
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HPV 16/18 with or without cytology, any cytology result excluding cancer -> 30 days.
What information does the grader need to: HPV genotype and cytology result or absence of cytology

Category or scenario: Primary screening: HPV other with cytology reporting suspicion or definite cancer
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HPV other with cytology reporting suspicion or definite cancer -> 10 days.

Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HPV other with cytology reporting ASC-H, HSIL, AIS, or glandular -> 30 days.

Category or scenario: Primary screening: second HPV other with no cytology or normal, ASC-US, LSIL >50
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Second HPV other with no cytology or cytology normal, ASC-US, LSIL >50 -> 3 months.
What information does the grader need to: Repeat count, HPV group, cytology, age split where used

Category or scenario: Primary screening: third HPV other with no cytology or normal, ASC-US, LSIL <50
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Third HPV other with no cytology or cytology normal, ASC-US, LSIL <50 -> 6 months.
What information does the grader need to: Repeat count, HPV group, cytology, age split where used

Category or scenario: Immune-deficient direct referral: no cytology
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Immune deficient with no cytology -> 3 months.

Category or scenario: Immune-deficient direct referral: cytology normal, ASC-US, or LSIL
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Immune deficient with cytology normal, ASC-US, LSIL -> 6 months.

Category or scenario: Abnormal appearance: clinical suspicion or definite cancer
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Abnormal cervical appearance with clinical suspicion or definite cancer -> 10 days.
What information does the grader need to: Cervical appearance and clinical concern

Category or scenario: Abnormal appearance: normal sample history including current sample
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Abnormal cervical appearance with normal sample history, including current sample -> 3 months.

Category or scenario: Other reasons: HPV not detected and suspicion of cancer
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HPV not detected and suspicion of cancer, with or without cytology -> 10 days.
What information does the grader need to: HPV result, cancer suspicion, cytology if present

Category or scenario: Other reasons: HPV not detected with ASC-H, HSIL, AIS, or glandular cytology
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HPV not detected with cytology reporting ASC-H, HSIL, AIS, or glandular -> 30 days.
What information does the grader need to: HPV result and cytology result

Category or scenario: Other reasons: other clinical assessment (ambiguous in guide)
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: The guide lists 'Other reason: Other clinical assessment' at 30 days, 3 months, and 6 months, but does not show the condition that differentiates these three timings. Please clarify the actual rule.
What information does the grader need to: Reason for referral and local clinical rule
Expected outcome or priority: Please confirm 30 days / 3 months / 6 months criteria

Category or scenario: Faster Cancer Treatment (FCT) pathway
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: The grading template includes an FCT field with three options: Confirmed cancer at grading, High suspicion of cancer at grading, No/Low suspicion of cancer at grading. Please confirm when each applies.
What information does the grader need to: Clinical findings, histology, imaging if relevant

Category or scenario: Ovestin prescribing
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: The grading template includes Ovestin prescribing options for patients who are amenorrhoeic, >50yo, or post-menopausal. Please confirm the rules for when each option applies.
What information does the grader need to: Patient age, menopausal status, breastfeeding, Depo use, hormone contraindication
Expected outcome or priority: Ovestin instruction to referrer -- please confirm rules

Category or scenario: NCSR notes
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: The grading template includes NCSR note options (published to Whaihua/Register, not applicable, internal referral note). Please confirm when each is used.
What information does the grader need to: NCSR registration status, referral type

Category or scenario: Grading template fields -- please confirm which are required
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: The current grading template appears to include: Status Reason, Priority, FCT, Clinic, HPV test, HPV Type, Cytology sample, Referrer's reason for referral, Genotype, Investigations, Category, Assessment of referral, Booking priority, Type, To be seen by SMO only, Ovestin, NCSR notes, Triage Notes (internal), Notes. Please mark which fields are required, which are optional, and which ones drive the grading decision.
What information does the grader need to: All of the above

Category or scenario: AUB -- no ultrasound within 12 months
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If no pelvic USS within 12 months: reject and send back to GP requesting re-referral with scan.
What information does the grader need to: Referral content, USS availability

Category or scenario: AUB -- ET >15mm or no recent endometrial sample, with or without adenomyosis
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If USS shows endometrial thickness >15mm and no pipelle or endometrial sample in last 6 months, with or without adenomyosis: P2 Menorrhagia.
What information does the grader need to: USS findings, endometrial thickness, biopsy history

Category or scenario: AUB -- USS suggestive of polyp
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If USS suggestive of polyp with or without dysmenorrhoea: P3 Hysteroscopy.
What information does the grader need to: USS findings, symptoms

Category or scenario: AUB -- ET <15mm, normal USS, but ongoing bleeding and tried medical management
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If ET <15mm and otherwise normal but intermenstrual or continuous bleeding >3 months and patient has tried medical management (Mirena, Provera, TXA, COC, POP), with or without dysmenorrhoea or adenomyosis: P3 Menorrhagia. If not tried medical management, suggest trying first.
What information does the grader need to: USS, bleeding duration, medications tried
Expected outcome or priority: P3 Menorrhagia (or suggest medical management first)

Category or scenario: AUB -- post-coital bleeding with normal smear (premenopausal)
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Post-coital bleeding with normal smear in premenopausal patient: does not need to be seen (Northern Region Agreement).
What information does the grader need to: Smear result, menopausal status
Expected outcome or priority: Does not need to be seen

Category or scenario: AUB -- small fibroid (<3cm) found incidentally on USS
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If USS shows fibroid <3cm with no other abnormalities and normal ET: decline with advice that fibroid is incidental, try medical management. P3 Gynae if already tried medical management.
What information does the grader need to: USS, fibroid size, ET, management tried
Expected outcome or priority: Decline (or P3 if tried medical management)

Category or scenario: AUB -- abnormal cervix with normal smear (SMO grading)
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If abnormal cervix with normal smear: P2 Gynae. SMO grading required.
What information does the grader need to: Cervical appearance, smear result

Category or scenario: PMB -- no USS within 6 months
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: No USS within 6 months: reject and ask to re-refer with USS (suggest POAC if unable to afford). Exception: clear historic abnormality with delay to review.
What information does the grader need to: USS availability, clinical history

Category or scenario: PMB -- single episode, USS <4mm
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Single episode PMB with USS ET <4mm polyp: suggest community pipelle if able, ovestin cream, and refer if recurrent PMB.
What information does the grader need to: PMB episodes, USS findings, ET
Expected outcome or priority: Suggest community pipelle and ovestin, re-refer if recurrent

Category or scenario: PMB -- one or more episodes, USS ET >=5mm
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: One or more episodes of PMB with USS ET >=5mm: HSC P1, Hysteroscopy Rapid Access Clinic.
What information does the grader need to: PMB episodes, USS findings, ET

Category or scenario: PMB -- multiple episodes but ET <5mm
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Multiple episodes of PMB but ET <5mm: HSC P1, RAC clinic.
What information does the grader need to: PMB episodes, USS findings, ET

Category or scenario: PMB -- USS shows other abnormalities (SMO grading)
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: If USS shows any other abnormalities: SMO-only grading, clinical judgement.
What information does the grader need to: USS findings

Category or scenario: Fibroids
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Fibroids >3cm with mass symptoms (urinary, bowel, pain) and/or hydronephrosis: P2 Gynae. Fibroids <3cm with mass symptoms: P3 Gynae (note to GP to explore other causes). Fibroids <3cm with no mass symptoms or AUB: decline, no follow-up scan needed.
What information does the grader need to: Fibroid size, symptoms, USS findings
Expected outcome or priority: P2 or P3 or Decline depending on size and symptoms

Category or scenario: Ovarian masses and cysts
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Probable benign ovarian cysts (simple or likely dermoid): Gynae P2. Complex adnexal masses that appear suspicious: SMO-only grading, order CT if >40, tumour markers all ages, HSC P1.
What information does the grader need to: Mass characteristics, imaging, tumour markers, age
Expected outcome or priority: P2 or HSC P1 (SMO only for suspicious)

Category or scenario: HSC P2 -- semi-urgent (cross-cutting category)
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: HSC P2 is an SMO-only category for referrals with concerning features that do not qualify for HSC P1 but should not wait the standard P2 timeframe. Examples: borderline ovarian cyst, recurrent PMB with normal histology, premenopausal with significantly increased ET. Tracked by Gynaecology Nurse Coordinator.
What information does the grader need to: Clinical judgement, imaging, histology
Expected outcome or priority: P2-HSC (SMO only, tracked by nurse coordinator)

Category or scenario: Pelvic pain
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: No USS: reject unless extensive endometriosis history. Pelvic pain >3 months with normal USS: P3. Abnormal USS with endometriomas >=5cm: P2. DIE on imaging: P2. Chronic pelvic pain fully investigated and gynae cause treated: decline, refer to Chronic Pain Service.
What information does the grader need to: USS, pain duration, prior treatment, imaging
Expected outcome or priority: P2 or P3 or Reject or Decline depending on findings

Category or scenario: Urogynaecology
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Multiple sub-pathways including mesh problems (P2, SMO), procidentia (P2), prolapse without procidentia (P3), prolapse with urinary retention (P2), physiotherapy referral (P2), pessary, incontinence (P3 for stress, reject for urge unless tried medications, reject for asymptomatic prolapse), previous TVT/sling (P2, SMO). Urogynae patient with PMB follows PMB grading.
What information does the grader need to: Presenting issue, examination findings, prior treatment, mesh history

Category or scenario: Fertility
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Decline and advise GP to refer directly to Northern Region Fertility Service (NRFS).
What information does the grader need to: Referral reason

Category or scenario: PCOS
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Virtual only. Women with PCOS not seen face-to-face. Refer GP to PCOS guidelines on Health Pathways. Refer for clinician advice if diagnosis unclear. SMO if fertility component.
What information does the grader need to: Symptoms, fertility concern, diagnosis clarity

Category or scenario: Cervical polyp
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Asymptomatic, <=2cm with normal smear: reject, GP to monitor. >=2cm with normal smear and symptoms (post-coital or intermenstrual bleeding): P3 Gynaecology.
What information does the grader need to: Polyp size, symptoms, smear result
Expected outcome or priority: Reject or P3 depending on size and symptoms

Category or scenario: Paediatric gynaecology and structural anomalies
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: SMO grading. Except menstrual disorders -- may be reviewed at Counties Manukau with named consultants. Young women with raised tumour markers and complex cysts go to FCT team unless clearly endometrioma. Otherwise transfer to Paediatric Gynaecology / Female Multi Clinic Te Toka Tumai.
What information does the grader need to: Age, presenting issue, imaging, tumour markers
Expected outcome or priority: SMO grading, possible transfer to paediatric service

Category or scenario: Pelvic tear
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: 3A: refer to WH physio. 3B / 3C / 4th degree: P3.
What information does the grader need to: Tear grade, symptoms

Category or scenario: Tubal ligation
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Tubal ligation counselling (MSC): P3.
What information does the grader need to: Referral reason

Category or scenario: Reject, return, or request-more-information rules
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Several categories require minimum evidence before grading (e.g. USS for AUB, PMB, pelvic pain). Referrals without required evidence should be returned to GP with a specific request. The service also has decline outcomes for conditions that do not warrant specialist review.
What information does the grader need to: Minimum investigations, referral completeness
Expected outcome or priority: Reject, return to GP, or decline with advice

Category or scenario: Escalation -- re-grading patients already on the waitlist
Our understanding of the rule or decisio: Patients already on a waitlist may be re-referred with updated clinical information. These must be re-graded and the booking team notified if priority changes.
What information does the grader need to: Updated referral, prior grading, new clinical information
